close_reason: Added jmap_server::server_fail_from_backend(&err) helper that returns JmapError::server_fail with a static 'internal error' description, dropping the backend error's Display text rather than echoing it onto the wire. Public const SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC exposes the static description for reference. Replaced 7 .map_err(|e| JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string())) call sites in crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs with the new helper. Tests: canary-leak proves the helper drops the backend Display text and the resulting wire description is exactly SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC; bound is Display + ?Sized so it works on String/&str/JmapBackend::Error/BackendSetError/etc. Filed JMAP-wlip.33 to propagate the helper to the ~203 analogous call sites in the 8 extension *-server crates per canonical-template rule.
description:
Trigger: any backend impl whose Error::Display output contains credential material, blob content, or PII shaped like an email address. Today: every generic handler in crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs (handle_get:30,55,60; handle_changes:99; handle_query:153,205; handle_query_changes:242) wraps backend errors with JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string()). That string lands in the wire-format JmapError.description field of the error invocation returned to the JMAP client at HTTP 200.

The new bd:JMAP-sc1b.100 security contract added in commit 8099de3 (crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:618-645) imposes a MUST-NOT on backend Error Display output. The contract is correct as far as it goes, but the contract is on the *backend implementor*. The handler is where the blast radius gets magnified — it sends the backend's Display text not just to operator logs (where a careful operator might redact) but to the JMAP client over HTTP.

A backend impl that accidentally violates the Display contract today produces:
  HTTP 200 → methodResponses[i] = ["error", {"type":"serverFail", "description":"<leaked secret>"}, callId]
…visible to any client that can dispatch a method whose backend call fails.

Right behaviour (defense-in-depth at the handler layer):
- handlers SHOULD construct serverFail without a description for unexpected backend errors that originated as Error::Other / Self::Error → operator-log the full text via tracing::error!, return JmapError::server_fail("internal error") to the wire. RFC 8620 §3.6.2 explicitly permits omitting description.
- handlers SHOULD only echo description for JmapError variants whose description is part of the API contract (limit, invalidArguments, invalidResultReference, etc. — methods that constructed the JmapError themselves with caller-meaningful detail).

This is a real defence: it changes a backend Display-contract bug from a *wire-format security incident* to a *server-side log issue*. The backend Display contract is necessary but insufficient on its own — handlers are the canonical leak path and need the matching guard.

Scope: applies to all five .map_err(|e| JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string())) call sites in handlers.rs plus any analog in extension *-server crates.
title: Generic handlers leak JmapBackend::Error Display verbatim into serverFail.description on the wire
